nodes.title: Hydraulic Systems
nodes.summary: Introduces the concept of hydraulic systems in aircraft, describing their purpose and basic operation.
objectives: Define an aircraft hydraulic system
Explain the role of hydraulic power in aircraft functions

nodes.title: Power Generation
nodes.summary: Covers the power‑generation portion of hydraulic systems, focusing on how hydraulic pressure is produced.
objectives: Describe methods of hydraulic power generation
Identify sources of hydraulic energy within an aircraft

nodes.title: Pumps
nodes.summary: Focuses on pumps as the primary devices for generating hydraulic pressure.
objectives: Explain pump operation principles
Classify different types of hydraulic pumps

nodes.title: Engine-Driven Pumps
nodes.summary: Details engine‑driven pumps, their integration with aircraft engines, and their function within the hydraulic system.
objectives: Describe how engine‑driven pumps operate
Recognize the role of engine‑driven pumps in system pressure maintenance

nodes.title: Electric Pumps
nodes.summary: This section introduces electric pumps, focusing on electric motor pumps that serve as backups when main engines are shut down and outlining their duty‑cycle limitations.
objectives: Identify electric pump types
Explain the backup function of electric motor pumps
Describe duty‑cycle limitations for electric motor pumps

nodes.title: Reservoirs
nodes.summary: The section covers fluid reservoirs and explains how they are pressurised using bleed air to prevent pump cavitation, especially at altitude.
objectives: Define a reservoir
Describe bleed‑air pressurisation of reservoirs
Explain how pressurisation prevents pump cavitation

nodes.title: Distribution
nodes.summary: This brief section introduces the concept of distribution within the system, establishing it as a separate functional area.
objectives: Recognize distribution as a system component

nodes.title: Valves
nodes.summary: The section provides an overview of valves, laying the groundwork for more detailed valve types later in the course.
objectives: Identify the role of valves in the system

nodes.title: Selector Valves
nodes.summary: The section examines selector valves, detailing the two main types—spool and rotary—and noting that they are typically solenoid‑operated.
objectives: Define selector valves
Differentiate spool‑type and rotary‑type selector valves
Explain how solenoid operation controls selector valves

nodes.title: Maintenance
nodes.summary: This section introduces the Maintenance module of the course, outlining its scope and relevance to overall system upkeep.
objectives: Identify the purpose of maintenance activities

nodes.title: Servicing
nodes.summary: This section presents the Servicing component, describing its role in routine equipment care and preparation for operation.
objectives: Recognize key servicing tasks

nodes.title: Fluid Handling
nodes.summary: This section covers basic fluid handling principles and provides specific safety precautions for working with Skydrol hydraulic fluid.
objectives: Explain fluid handling procedures
Apply Skydrol safety measures

properties.heading: Hydraulic Systems
properties.text:
Hydraulic Systems

Introduces the concept of hydraulic systems in aircraft, describing their purpose and basic operation.

Objectives:
- Define an aircraft hydraulic system
- Explain the role of hydraulic power in aircraft functions

properties.heading: Power Generation
properties.text:
Power Generation

Covers the power‑generation portion of hydraulic systems, focusing on how hydraulic pressure is produced.

Objectives:
- Describe methods of hydraulic power generation
- Identify sources of hydraulic energy within an aircraft

properties.heading: Pumps
properties.text:
Pumps

Focuses on pumps as the primary devices for generating hydraulic pressure.

Objectives:
- Explain pump operation principles
- Classify different types of hydraulic pumps

properties.heading: Engine-Driven Pumps
properties.text:
Engine-Driven Pumps

Details engine‑driven pumps, their integration with aircraft engines, and their function within the hydraulic system.

Objectives:
- Describe how engine‑driven pumps operate
- Recognize the role of engine‑driven pumps in system pressure maintenance

properties.heading: Electric Pumps
properties.text:
Electric Pumps

This section introduces electric pumps, focusing on electric motor pumps that serve as backups when main engines are shut down and outlining their duty‑cycle limitations.

Objectives:
- Identify electric pump types
- Explain the backup function of electric motor pumps
- Describe duty‑cycle limitations for electric motor pumps

properties.heading: Reservoirs
properties.text:
Reservoirs

The section covers fluid reservoirs and explains how they are pressurised using bleed air to prevent pump cavitation, especially at altitude.

Objectives:
- Define a reservoir
- Describe bleed‑air pressurisation of reservoirs
- Explain how pressurisation prevents pump cavitation

properties.heading: Distribution
properties.text:
Distribution

This brief section introduces the concept of distribution within the system, establishing it as a separate functional area.

Objectives:
- Recognize distribution as a system component

properties.heading: Valves
properties.text:
Valves

The section provides an overview of valves, laying the groundwork for more detailed valve types later in the course.

Objectives:
- Identify the role of valves in the system

properties.heading: Selector Valves
properties.text:
Selector Valves

The section examines selector valves, detailing the two main types—spool and rotary—and noting that they are typically solenoid‑operated.

Objectives:
- Define selector valves
- Differentiate spool‑type and rotary‑type selector valves
- Explain how solenoid operation controls selector valves

properties.heading: Maintenance
properties.text:
Maintenance

This section introduces the Maintenance module of the course, outlining its scope and relevance to overall system upkeep.

Objectives:

properties.heading: Servicing

Servicing

properties.text:

Objectives:

- Apply Skydrol safety measures
